name: Classynt Schools
author: classynt

sections.description:
Classynt Schools helps a school run results, staff and students day to day, without spreadsheets. It is built to fit different countries and school systems: you choose how your academic year is divided, what is assessed and how it is graded.

School setup

  • School name, motto, address, contact details and logo
  • Report accent colour and head teacher sign-off (signature image or name and date)
  • Academic periods of your choice: terms, semesters, trimesters, quarters, or your own names
  • Assessment components you define for each period (for example coursework, midterm and exam), with maximum scores and ready-made presets
  • Configurable grading scale, with presets
  • Sessions, classes, sections and subjects

Student management

  • Add and manage students, with automatic PIN generation for portal login
  • Arrange the student list alphabetically by first name or by date added; your choice is remembered
  • Sections within each class, which can be removed without removing the class

Student result portal

  • Public shortcode: [classynt_result_portal]
  • Students sign in with an admission number and a PIN
  • Print-optimised report card: subject scores, attendance, psychomotor and affective ratings, comments and sign-off
  • Report text is translation-ready

Results workspace

  • Enter results and report details for a student on one page
  • Session, period and class filters with quick roster loading

Staff and teacher portal

  • Staff sign in with a Staff ID and PIN; no WordPress user account is required
  • Teachers only see the classes, sections and subjects assigned to them
  • Enter results and report details from the teacher dashboard
  • Staff and assignment management, including per-section access restriction

Pro

Classynt Pro adds:

  • Report page layout: choose which sections appear (attendance, rating sections, comment boxes), their order, titles and labels, add your own rating sections and comment boxes, and decide which boxes staff may edit. The same layout is used on the Results page, the staff dashboard, the printed report and the student portal
  • Promotion to the next class and session, with an optional pass-mark condition; earlier results stay with the class and session they belong to
  • Per-session fee gate: mark a student Paid or Outstanding and the portal holds Outstanding results, with bulk controls per class
  • More report card templates: Academic, Comprehensive, Progress, Competency and Transcript
  • Result locking per session, period and class
  • Audit trail of result changes
  • Extra staff capabilities, including adding and editing students and promoting classes from the teacher dashboard
  • Classroom Suite: announcements to the whole school, a class, a section or a subject, with scheduling, pinning, read receipts and an optional emailed copy. Assignments (set work, hand in online, grade with feedback) and a past-questions library (PDF papers students can search and download) are in Pro; timed computer-based exams (question bank, random questions, several subjects in one exam with free movement between them, automatic marking, scores sent to the results) are in Pro too, all in the same Classroom Suite
  • Text-message (SMS) password reset for students, parents and staff; people choose Email or SMS on the reset screen

Pro functionality is not included in this WordPress.org build.

External services

This plugin uses Freemius, a licensing and software-update platform, to manage optional license activation for the Pro version and (only if you choose to opt in) anonymous usage analytics that help us improve the plugin.

No data is sent to Freemius automatically when the plugin is activated. On first activation you’re shown a one-time opt-in screen with two options — “Skip” or “Allow & Continue” — and nothing is transmitted to Freemius until you make that choice. If you click “Skip”, no usage data is shared and the plugin works fully. If you click “Allow & Continue”, or if you later connect a license or account from the Account page, the following is sent: your site URL, WordPress and PHP version, this plugin’s version, and (for connecting an account) the name and email of the WordPress user connecting it. No student, teacher, parent, or school data stored by this plugin (results, attendance, admission numbers, PINs, etc.) is ever sent to Freemius or any other third party — all of that stays in your own WordPress database.

Pro version only, and only if you turn it on: SMS password/PIN reset. When an administrator selects Twilio or Africa’s Talking and enters their own account details, the plugin sends the recipient’s phone number and a short text containing a one-time code to that provider when someone asks for an SMS reset (and to the number you type when you press “Send test SMS”). Nothing is sent until you choose a provider and enable it, and no results or other school data is included.
Twilio: https://www.twilio.com — Terms: https://www.twilio.com/legal/tos — Privacy: https://www.twilio.com/legal/privacy
Africa’s Talking: https://africastalking.com — Terms: https://africastalking.com/terms — Privacy: https://africastalking.com/privacy

Pro version only, and only if you turn it on: online admission payments. When an administrator enables Stripe, PayPal or Paystack and a parent chooses to pay online, the plugin sends the fee amount, currency, the parent’s email address and the application reference to that provider, and the parent completes payment on the provider’s own page. The plugin later asks the provider whether the payment succeeded. Nothing is sent until you enable a provider and a parent starts a payment.
Stripe: https://stripe.com — Terms: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa — Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy
PayPal: https://www.paypal.com — Terms: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/paypal/useragreement-full — Privacy: https://www.paypal.com/privacy
Paystack: https://paystack.com — Terms: https://paystack.com/terms — Privacy: https://paystack.com/privacy

This service is provided by Freemius Inc.

Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/classynt-schools, or install through the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen.
  3. Open Classynt → Settings → School Setup and enter your school’s details, academic periods, assessment components and grading scale.
  4. Create a session; its periods are created for you.
  5. Create classes and subjects, and assign subjects to classes.
  6. Add students; a login PIN is generated automatically.
  7. Place [classynt_result_portal] on any page, or let the plugin create one for you.
sections.faq:
Does it work for schools outside Africa?

Yes. Nothing is fixed to one country: you choose terms, semesters, trimesters, quarters or your own period names, define your own assessment components and set your own grading scale.

Can students and staff reset a forgotten PIN or password themselves?

Yes, if you turn it on (Setup > Sign-in). Staff receive a one-time link at their own email address. Students receive it at their own email address if you recorded one, otherwise through a parent or guardian who agreed to email contact (Parents and guardians on the student’s edit screen). Parents use the email on their account. An administrator can always reset anyone from the Students or Staff screen. Email delivery depends on your hosting; use the “Send me a test email” button, and an SMTP plugin if mail does not arrive.

What are temporary PINs?

Optional, off by default. In Classynt > Setup & region profiles > Sign-in you can ask students and staff to choose their own PIN the first time they sign in with a PIN an administrator issued. When you create or reset a PIN, it is shown once on screen and is not kept in the page address.

Can teachers post announcements?

Yes, in Classynt Pro. Teachers post notices from the staff portal to the classes and subjects they are assigned to. Administrators can post to the whole school from Advanced Workflow > Classroom Suite. Students and parents read them under Notices on their portal.

Can parents see their child’s results?

Yes, if you turn on the parent portal in Classynt > Setup > Sign-in. A parent signs in with their own account and sees each linked child read-only. You can create the account on the student edit screen, or the student can make a one-time code for the parent to enter. Parents see results only after you release them, and each visit is logged.

Do students need a WordPress account?

No. Students sign in with an admission number and PIN.

Can teachers log in without a WordPress account?

Yes. Staff sign in with a Staff ID and PIN issued by the administrator, and only see the classes and subjects assigned to them.

Can I set up Classynt for my country’s grading system?

Yes. Open Classynt > Setup, choose a region profile (or import one), preview exactly what will change, and confirm. A profile sets the periods for new sessions, the assessment components, the grading bands, class positions and the result template. The example profiles are starting points, not official standards, so check the bands against your own school or district. You can undo the last profile you applied.

Can I decide when students see their results?

Yes. Open Classynt > Release results, choose the session and period, tick the classes (or Select all) and press Release selected. Until a class is released, its students see “Result not released yet”, even if teachers have entered scores. You can mark a class as not released again at any time.

What happens if someone guesses PINs?

After 5 wrong PINs the student or staff sign-in is locked for a few minutes, and repeat locks last longer. Administrators can see and unlock locked sign-ins on the Classynt > Login security screen. To limit guessing, Classynt stores a keyed hash of the typed Admission number or Staff ID and of the visitor’s IP address (never the IP address itself) for a short time.

What happens to a student’s old results after promotion?

Promotion is a Classynt Pro feature. Earlier results stay with the class and session they belong to, students can still view them in the portal by choosing the earlier session, and rankings and averages for that session are not affected.

Can I change which report sections and comment boxes are used?

Yes, in Classynt Pro, using the Report page layout settings. The free version uses the standard layout.

How do I stop a student from seeing a result before fees are paid?

This is a Classynt Pro feature. Mark the student’s session as “Outstanding” on the Results screen and the portal holds the report until it is marked “Paid”.
sections.changelog:
1.19.0

  • New (Pro): staff roles. A new Staff roles screen lets you create roles and tick exactly what each one may do in the staff portal. A head teacher or principal can now sign in with a Staff ID and PIN, see every class, and write the head teacher’s comment on report cards without a WordPress login. Built-in roles: Teacher (unchanged), Result officer (unchanged) and Head teacher / Principal. Give a role to a person on the Teachers screen.
  • New (Pro): exams can mix several subjects. Add one row per subject and students get a tab for each subject, so they can skip a subject, answer another and go back. Each subject’s score goes to that subject’s own results row when you send scores to the results.
  • Improved (Pro): the exam question screen is rewritten in plain language (“Let the system choose questions at random”), with a short how-it-works box, a summary of the paper, one card per subject, and the question type, topic and Easy/Medium/Hard filters tucked under “Narrow it down”.
  • Fixed (Pro): exams that students had already started had no Delete button. There is now always a Delete button; for a started exam it is “Delete exam and student work” and tells you how many students’ work will go. Scores already sent to the results are not removed. Delete buttons now also ask before deleting.
  • New (Pro): admissions are flexible. Add your own questions (short or long answer, choose one, tick all that apply, date, email address, phone number, number, web address, tick box) with optional help text, up to 30 per round. Add any documents you need (up to 20), choose whether each accepts a PDF or picture, a picture only (for a passport photograph) or a PDF only, and add a note for parents.
  • Improved (Pro): when a test SMS fails, Classynt now shows the provider’s reason and, for Twilio, what to do about it. Setup help explains the Account SID, Auth Token, sender number, trial accounts and country permissions.
  • Fixed: the “Only students who have passed” option on the teacher portal promotion list showed a raw code instead of the greater-or-equal sign.
  • Fixed (Pro): on the exam screen the subject tabs of a multi-subject exam were squashed to a thin strip, so the subject names could not be seen or clicked. They now keep their full size and stay at the top while the question scrolls.
  • Fixed (Pro): questions and answers written with double asterisks around a word, such as ALLEVIATE, showed the asterisks on the exam screen. The word now appears in bold.
  • Fixed: every item in the Plugin Check report. Screens now read what to show (tab, class, session) through one validated helper, every admin action checks its nonce and permission before reading any input, PINs and passwords are read without being altered, database lookups on the admin, parent and sign-in screens go through the plugin’s own data classes, the profile download and the parent password emails no longer use unprefixed constants or hooks, and a debug log line was removed. Parent password emails now say the link expires after a short time instead of quoting a number of hours.

1.18.0

  • New (Pro): exam formats. Start a new exam from a ready-made practice format: quick quiz, class test, end-of-term, and formats modelled on UTME, WASSCE, SAT, ACT, AP, JEE Main, NEET, MDCAT, IGCSE-style and IB-style papers. They are practice formats, not official exams; every number (time, questions, scoring, penalty) can be changed before saving, and schools can add their own with the classynt_sr_cbt_presets filter.
  • New (Pro): more question types: number answers (with a tolerance and comma or point decimals), short written answers, and essays that you mark by hand. Results stay provisional until every essay is marked.
  • New (Pro): exam sections. Group random draws under a section name (for example Reading or Paper 1); questions are shuffled inside each section and a draw can use another subject you teach or one question type.
  • New (Pro): scoring options: a penalty for wrong choice answers (never below zero, blanks lose nothing) and “score out of” any number, such as 100 or 400.
  • New (Pro): choose when students see results: right after hand-in, when the exam closes, or when you release them. Essay marking queue and a release button are on the results screen.
  • New (Pro): question analysis for each exam (how many got each question right, skipped, and which questions look too easy, too hard or mis-keyed).
  • New (Pro): optional exam access code and allowed network addresses (for example a computer lab). Attention signals (left full screen, switched tab, lost connection) are recorded for you to review; they are hints, not proof.
  • New (Pro): download your question bank as a CSV file to back it up or share it, and import number, fill-in and essay questions from a file.
  • Improved (Pro): written answers save as the student types, with a word count for essays, and the result screen has an animated score ring (still, for people who prefer reduced motion).
  • Improved (Pro): the exam question picker lists every question with search and select-all.

1.17.1

  • Fixed: new installs and new users no longer open in the full-screen admin layout. It has been removed, and the normal WordPress admin is used everywhere.
  • Fixed (Pro): parent sign-in. The parent portal now switches itself on when a parent account is created (from the admin or on enrolment), and the sign-in page is never cached and explains an expired page clearly.
  • Fixed: the “saving” animation no longer stays on screen after a file download, such as the question CSV template.
  • Fixed (Pro): an exam with no opening time now opens as soon as it is published, and the form shows the site time zone and current time so scheduled times are clear.
  • Improved (Pro): an exam can have up to 2000 questions, and the picker lists every question in the subject instead of only the newest 20.
  • Improved (Pro): parents of applicants choose all their documents and send them with one button; each file is checked on its own and anything left empty can be sent later.
  • Changed: the minimum PHP version is now 8.2 (was 8.3), for wider hosting and Freemius deployment support.

1.17.0

  • Requirement: Classynt now needs WordPress 6.4 or newer, and the bundled Freemius SDK is updated to 2.13.5.
  • New (Pro): online payments for admissions. Parents can pay the application or acceptance fee by card or bank on Stripe, PayPal or Paystack. Each payment is checked directly with the provider, the amount and currency must match the fee set on the round, and a numbered receipt is issued once. Secret keys are best kept in wp-config.php; keys typed in the settings are stored encrypted and never shown again.
  • New (Pro): on an accepted application, the Payments box now has an Enrol this student button once any acceptance fee is settled.
  • Requirement: Classynt now needs PHP 8.2 or newer. The code was brought up to date for it (strict types, native string functions, and old-PHP fall-backs removed). Ask your host to switch the site to PHP 8.2 or newer before updating.
  • New (Pro): admissions documents. Each round can ask for documents (for example a birth certificate) and attach a form for parents to download. Parents upload PDF, JPG or PNG files from their private link; staff accept them or send them back with a note.
  • New (Pro): admissions fees and receipts. Parents see how to pay (bank transfer, cash or any way you set up), report their payment with proof, and staff confirm it to issue a numbered receipt that can include an optional tax line, or send it back with a reason. The fee always comes from the round, never from what a parent types.
  • Improved (Pro): after a parent uploads a document, reports a payment or answers an offer, the page returns to their application, so reloading it does not send the form again.
  • New (Pro): online admissions. Put [classynt_admissions] on a page and parents can apply to an open intake round: the child, the parent, your own extra questions and a consent tick box. Parents get a private link by email to follow progress, accept an offer or withdraw, and can ask for the link again.
  • New (Pro): Classynt Schools > Admissions for administrators. Review applications by stage, add private notes, offer places, enrol accepted children as students (temporary PIN that must be changed at first sign-in, guardian saved, parent portal account created), manage intake rounds and download a CSV.
  • New (Pro): admissions privacy. Declined and withdrawn applications are removed automatically after the number of months you choose, and WordPress personal-data export and erase cover applications.

1.16.3

  • Design: the student, teacher and parent portals, and the Pro screens inside them (notices, assignments, past questions, exams and performance), now share the same look as the admin screens, with cards, tiles, clear tables and a readable exam page. They are tidy and fully usable on a phone: report cards, score entry, rating tables and the result preview no longer need sideways swiping, and no text or button touches the edge of the screen.
  • New: full-screen portals. The sign-in screens and the portals open full screen, without the website’s header and footer, with a slim bar that has a Back button and a Website home button. Turn this off under Classynt > Plugin settings > Full-screen portals if you prefer your theme’s layout.
  • New: the panel beside every sign-in form now rotates through three short messages every five seconds. Visitors can tap a dot to choose one, it pauses while the mouse or keyboard is on it, and it stays still for people who ask their device for reduced motion.
  • New: animated artwork on the student, teacher and parent sign-in screens. Three scenes change with the words every five seconds: an orbiting ring, a report card that fills in and earns an A, and a ringing bell with notices arriving. They also run on phones, and stay still for people who ask their device for reduced motion.
  • Improved: one loading animation everywhere, with wording for what is happening: “Preparing your student space”, “Opening exams”, “Opening the report card”, “Saving scores” and so on. It had not been loading on portal pages before.
  • Fix: exams could not be started and assignment or past-paper forms lost fields inside the student portal, because the page filter removed their data and form attributes.
  • Fix: on a phone the Back button no longer sits on top of the CLASSYNT label, and the teacher sign-in headline no longer overlaps it.
  • New (Pro): computer-based exams are now a full exam room. A start screen shows the number of questions, time and rules. The exam then opens full screen with a timer, a question list coloured by answered, flagged and unanswered, Flag for review, keyboard shortcuts (arrow keys, A to H) and a review screen before hand-in. It works on phones, where the question list becomes a drawer.
  • New (Pro): a simple calculator (add, subtract, multiply, divide) is available during every exam.
  • New (Pro): exams can be locked to full screen, and it is on by default. If a student leaves full screen, switches tab or app, or closes or reloads the page, the exam is handed in automatically and the teacher sees why. Phones that cannot show a page full screen are watched for leaving the exam instead. Switch it off per exam in the exam form.
  • New (Pro): teachers and administrators can add many questions at once from a CSV file, with a sample file to download, a step-by-step guide and an optional “Watch the video tutorial” link that the administrator sets.
  • New (Pro): clearer exam screens for teachers and administrators: summary figures, exam cards with status, and a form in three short sections.
  • New (Pro): the student portal shows a notice number on Exams for exams that are open or coming up and not yet taken.
  • New (Pro): the teacher “Result access” section now shows the paid / outstanding switch to Pro schools. It was showing the upgrade message by mistake.
  • Fix: the animation no longer appears on every small click. It shows for sign-in and sign-out, when moving to another screen, and for slow saves only.
  • Fix: the parent sign-in could silently fail on pages built with a page builder. Parent, teacher and student pages are now recognised reliably, which also fixes full-screen mode and the loading text on those pages.
  • Fix: button text could be unreadable (blue on blue, or white on white), including the New assignment and Cancel buttons and buttons in the admin area.

1.16.2

  • Design: every Classynt screen now shares one look. Sessions, Classes, Subjects, Students, Login security and Release results use the same dark page header as the dashboard, section titles, status badges and empty states; Login security and Release results were plain text before. Page content no longer touches the right edge of the screen, and keyboard focus is clearly visible.

1.16.1

  • Fix: the dashboard’s in-depth performance analysis no longer disappears silently. When the school has no academic session yet, or the chosen period has no completed results, the panel now stays on the page and says why, instead of looking as if it was missing from the plugin. (The analysis counts only students who have a result for every subject.)

1.16.0

  • Pro: Exams (CBT). Teachers (staff portal) and administrators build a question bank (single answer, several answers, true/false; subject, topic and difficulty) and set a timed exam for a class, a section and a subject. An exam can use fixed questions, random draws (for example 10 Algebra questions) or both, with questions and options shuffled for each student. Students open the new Exams tile, start when the exam is open, and the page saves answers as they go, counts down against the server clock and hands in by itself when time is up. Marking is automatic and all-or-nothing for multiple-answer questions.
  • Pro: built for a whole class starting at once. Each attempt is locked to one window, so a second browser tab or device cannot overwrite it; answers are kept on the device and re-sent if the connection drops; the answer key is never sent to the browser; an exam that is not handed in is closed automatically after its time (a background task every five minutes plus a check whenever the exam is opened). If a site blocks the WordPress REST API, the exam page uses admin-ajax instead.
  • Pro: results and scores. Teachers see who has started and handed in, download the results as CSV, and can let a student try again. After reviewing, a teacher sends the scores to a result column; locked or already released results are never changed, and scores that already exist are kept unless you choose to replace them. Whether students see their own score after hand-in is set per exam.
  • Pro: questions already used by an exam are locked, and an exam with attempts cannot have its questions changed or be deleted, so results always match what students saw.
  • Fix: a teacher can now see assignments that an administrator set for their class and subject, and the files students upload for them (previously only the teacher who set the work could see its hand-ins).
  • Changed: the Classroom Suite preview in the free version now lists all four Pro features (announcements, assignments, past questions, exams) without “coming soon”.
  • Uninstall removes the exam tables, the setting and the scheduled task when “delete data on uninstall” is on.

1.15.1

  • Pro: Past questions. Teachers (staff portal) and administrators add past papers as PDF files, up to 10 at a time, for a class, a section or a subject (administrators can also choose the whole school), with an optional year and exam type. Students open the new Past questions tile to search, filter by subject, year and exam type, sort, and download; parents see the same list. Teachers can only add papers for their own classes and subjects and can delete only their own. Downloads are counted.
  • Pro: past papers use the same private file storage as Assignments (random file names, signed links that expire after 15 minutes). Only real PDF files are accepted, and one bad file stops the whole batch so nothing is half-saved.
  • Uninstall removes the past questions table and its setting when “delete data on uninstall” is on.

1.15.0

  • New: students can have their own optional email address and phone number (student edit screen). A student who has them can reset a forgotten PIN or password without help; a student without them is reset only through a parent or guardian, or by an administrator.
  • New: the reset screen lets the person choose how to receive it, Email or SMS (SMS is Pro), for students, teachers and parents alike. With only one method switched on there is nothing to choose and the screen stays as simple as before.
  • New: parents can reset their password by SMS (Pro) as well as by email. A parent’s phone is taken from the number saved on their account (optional field when you add a portal account) or from a guardian record with the same email that agreed to SMS.
  • Changed: “Parents and guardians” is now one section on the student edit screen, with Contact details and Portal sign-in accounts together, instead of two separate sections.
  • Changed: Setup > Sign-in explains how to set up SMS step by step.
  • Pro: Assignments. Teachers (staff portal) and administrators set work for a class, a section and a subject, with instructions, up to 5 attached files, a due date, an optional maximum score, and a choice of typed answer, file upload, both, or none. Students hand in from the new Assignments tile; parents can see the work read-only. Teachers see who has handed in, grade with feedback, and reopen graded work. Late work is marked, or refused if you prefer. Teachers can only set work for their own classes and subjects. Grades are for feedback and are not copied into term results.
  • Pro: files for the Classroom Suite are stored in a private folder with random names and are served only through a signed link that expires after 15 minutes. Allowed: PDF, JPG, PNG, TXT, DOC(X), XLS(X), PPT(X), up to 8 MB each (or your server’s limit). On nginx servers the folder’s .htaccess deny rule is ignored, so the random names and signed links are what protect the files.
  • Uninstall removes the new tables, the private folder and parents’ saved phone numbers when “delete data on uninstall” is on.

1.14.2

  • Fix: an admission number typed on the keyboard now matches the same number pasted from a document, chat or PDF. Those sources often swap the plain hyphen for look-alikes (non-breaking hyphen, en dash, minus sign) or add invisible characters and non-breaking spaces, so the two looked the same but did not match and sign-in said the details were wrong.
  • Admission numbers are now cleaned of those characters whenever they are saved (admin, teacher dashboard) and whenever they are looked up (student sign-in, PIN/password reset by email or SMS, score import). Letter case is kept.
  • Admission numbers already saved with look-alike characters are cleaned once when you update. A number that would then match another student’s is left as it was, and the action is written to the audit log.

1.14.1

  • Pro: Announcements now live inside Advanced Workflow > Classroom Suite, the same page as the Classroom Suite preview, instead of a separate menu item. Old bookmarks are redirected. The free version shows the Pro preview on that page.
  • Pro: announcements have a formatting editor (bold, italic, lists, links) for administrators, and a light toolbar for teachers in the staff portal. Teachers can save, edit, archive and delete notices without the page reloading.
  • New: the parent portal has its own sign-in, “forgot password” and “choose a password” screens in the Classynt style (a warm orange design with its own wording), all on the parent page. Parents are never sent to the WordPress login screen. Reset links, new-account password links and password rules work the same way as for teachers and students. Wrong-password lock-out applies to parents too.
  • New: South Africa region preset (four terms, seven-point achievement scale shown as percentage and level) and a “4 Terms” period choice. The preset is a starting point: confirm the split and pass mark with your school.
  • New: optional default country calling code (School Setup > Contact). With it, phone numbers can be typed the local way (for example 082 123 4567) and are stored internationally. Without it, the + form is still required.
  • Fix: the plugin name in the main file is now “Classynt Schools” (it said “Classynt Schools Pro”), so the free package no longer ends in “Pro”.
  • Changed: the Classroom Suite preview now lists Past questions, and every Classroom Suite feature (announcements, assignments, past questions, exams) is Pro.

1.14.0

  • Pro: Announcements. Administrators and teachers post notices to the whole school, a class, a section or a subject, and choose whether students, parents or both see them.
  • Schedule a start and end time, pin a notice to the top, archive or delete it. Students and parents see them under Notices, with a “New” marker and an unread badge on the tile. Administrators see how many people have read each notice.
  • Teachers (staff portal) can only post to the classes, sections and subjects they are assigned to, and can only change their own notices.
  • Optional emailed copy to guardians who agreed to email contact (off until you turn it on in Advanced Workflow > Classroom Suite). Emails go out in batches of 40 through your site’s mail system, one per address.
  • Notice text is cleaned to a short list of safe tags. Dates are stored in UTC and shown in your site’s timezone.
  • Privacy: a parent’s notice read receipts are included in WordPress personal data export and erase.
  • Uninstall removes the announcement tables and any scheduled email batches when “delete data on uninstall” is on.

1.13.0

  • New: student portal home with tiles (Results and My performance now; Assignments and Notices appear when those features are added). New installs start on it; existing schools keep opening the result page until you choose “Home page with tiles” in Setup > Sign-in.
  • New: My performance. A student sees their average, class average, position (only if class positions are on), strengths, focus areas, how each subject compares with the class, and their average by period. It stays hidden until the class’s results are released.
  • New: parent portal (off by default; switch it on in Setup > Sign-in). Parents sign in with their own account and see each linked child read-only, with a child switcher, the same release rules as students, and a privacy notice to accept first.
  • New: link a parent by the school (Parent portal accounts on the student edit screen: creates an account or links an existing one and emails a password link) or by the student (Link a parent makes a one-time code that expires after 48 hours; five wrong codes lock that parent out for an hour).
  • New: access log. The student edit screen shows who opened the child’s information and when; entries older than a year are removed.
  • Privacy: parent accounts and their log are included in WordPress personal data export and erase, and are removed when the account is deleted.
  • Uninstall now also removes the new parent tables, the Parent role and several older leftover settings when “delete data on uninstall” is on.

1.12.0

  • Pro: three new result designs. Standards-based (a level and meaning for each subject, work habits kept apart, no totals or positions), GPA Transcript (credits, grade points, period and cumulative GPA, grading key) and Narrative (a holistic progress card with no marks).
  • New: Credits for each subject (Subjects screen), used by the GPA transcript.
  • New region presets (editable): United States high school (4.0 GPA), India CBSE-style 9-point scale, United Kingdom GCSE-style 9 to 1, Kenya CBC-style levels. Percentage cut-offs are illustrative; check them against your authority.
  • The United States elementary and Kenya presets now select the standards-based design.

1.11.0

  • New: sign in with a password instead of a PIN (Classynt > Setup > Sign-in). Nobody is locked out when you switch: each person signs in once with their current PIN, then chooses a password. Switching back to PIN works too. Minimum length is adjustable (default 8); long passphrases are allowed and common passwords are refused.
  • New: parents and guardians on each student (name, relationship, email, phone in international format, and whether they agreed to email or SMS contact).
  • New: optional reset of a forgotten PIN or password by an emailed one-time link (off by default). Staff are emailed at their own address; students through a guardian. Links work once, expire in one hour and are rate limited; the reply never reveals whether an account exists.
  • New: “Send me a test email” button, and email problems are shown in Setup.
  • Pro: optional reset by a 6-digit SMS code through Twilio or Africa’s Talking, using your own account. Off until you enter your details.

1.10.1

  • New: optional “choose your own PIN” at first sign-in for students and staff (off by default; existing accounts are not affected).
  • Security: a newly issued or reset PIN is now shown once from the server and is no longer placed in the page address.
  • New PINs must avoid repeated digits, sequences and repeated pairs.

1.10.0

  • New: Setup & region profiles (free). Choose a profile to set your periods, assessment components, grading bands, class positions and result template in one step. Preview the changes, confirm, and undo if needed. Nothing changes until you confirm.
  • Includes example profiles for Nigeria (A1-F9, three terms) and the United States elementary schools (four quarters). Import and export profiles as JSON to share a setup.
  • Safe by design: existing sessions keep their periods, periods that already have scores keep their assessment components, and scores are never changed.

1.9.18

  • New: Release results (free for everyone). Students see a class’s results only after an administrator releases them, one class or many at once, from Classynt > Release results. Until then they see “Result not released yet” (or “Result not available” when nothing has been entered).
  • Results that students could already see before this update stay released, so nothing disappears after updating.
  • The Pro fee hold still works on its own: a held-back student stays held back after their class is released.

1.9.17

  • Security: student and staff portal sign-in now locks after 5 wrong PINs (5, 15, 60, then 240 minutes on repeats). A shared school network gets a higher limit. Locked and unknown accounts show the same message.
  • New “Login security” screen to see locked sign-ins and unlock them. Locks are also recorded in the audit log.
  • Dashboard: the session, period, class and student pickers now load only when you press the button.

1.9.16

  • Dashboard: Results progress now follows the academic period that has results (it no longer reads an empty latest term), with a session and period picker.
  • Dashboard: in-depth school and student performance analysis for everyone – class comparison, subjects, grade distribution, trend, top students, students needing support and a student explorer. Pass mark setting.
  • Student and teacher sign-in screens share one standard layout, each keeping its own accent colour.
  • Removed the non-functional “Remember this device” option.

1.9.14

  • Students: “Arrange by” (first name or date added), remembered per user.
  • Classes: a section can be deleted without deleting its class.
  • Results: rankings and class averages use the class a student was in for that session, so promotions no longer change earlier results.
  • Academic periods are configurable: terms, semesters, trimesters, quarters or your own names.
  • Translation: the Results & Report Details page and roster are translatable.
  • Pro: Report page layout. Choose the sections, order, titles, labels, comment boxes and rating sections used on the Results page, staff dashboard, printed report and student portal.
  • Results page: notice explaining the report page layout setting.
  • Plugins screen: Tutorials & Guides link.
  • Plugin Check fixes: output escaping, stylesheet versioning, plugin name.

1.9.13

  • Printing fits on one page; PIN notices; teacher section selection and portal subject fixes; cleaner Settings layout.

1.9.12

  • Mobile printing fix; “Result not available” message; PIN show/hide icon; per-class subject selection for teachers.

1.9.11

  • WordPress.org review follow-up and compliance fixes, including the verified Freemius external-services disclosure and an upstream Freemius SDK debug-page fix.

short_description: School management and report cards for any country: students, staff, results, grading, and student and teacher portals.
description:
Classynt Schools helps a school run results, staff and students day to day, without spreadsheets. It is built to fit different countries and school systems: you choose how your academic year is divided, what is assessed and how it is graded.

School setup

  • School name, motto, address, contact details and logo
  • Report accent colour and head teacher sign-off (signature image or name and date)
  • Academic periods of your choice: terms, semesters, trimesters, quarters, or your own names
  • Assessment components you define for each period (for example coursework, midterm and exam), with maximum scores and ready-made presets
  • Configurable grading scale, with presets
  • Sessions, classes, sections and subjects

Student management

  • Add and manage students, with automatic PIN generation for portal login
  • Arrange the student list alphabetically by first name or by date added; your choice is remembered
  • Sections within each class, which can be removed without removing the class

Student result portal

  • Public shortcode: [classynt_result_portal]
  • Students sign in with an admission number and a PIN
  • Print-optimised report card: subject scores, attendance, psychomotor and affective ratings, comments and sign-off
  • Report text is translation-ready

Results workspace

  • Enter results and report details for a student on one page
  • Session, period and class filters with quick roster loading

Staff and teacher portal

  • Staff sign in with a Staff ID and PIN; no WordPress user account is required
  • Teachers only see the classes, sections and subjects assigned to them
  • Enter results and report details from the teacher dashboard
  • Staff and assignment management, including per-section access restriction

Pro

Classynt Pro adds:

  • Report page layout: choose which sections appear (attendance, rating sections, comment boxes), their order, titles and labels, add your own rating sections and comment boxes, and decide which boxes staff may edit. The same layout is used on the Results page, the staff dashboard, the printed report and the student portal
  • Promotion to the next class and session, with an optional pass-mark condition; earlier results stay with the class and session they belong to
  • Per-session fee gate: mark a student Paid or Outstanding and the portal holds Outstanding results, with bulk controls per class
  • More report card templates: Academic, Comprehensive, Progress, Competency and Transcript
  • Result locking per session, period and class
  • Audit trail of result changes
  • Extra staff capabilities, including adding and editing students and promoting classes from the teacher dashboard
  • Classroom Suite: announcements to the whole school, a class, a section or a subject, with scheduling, pinning, read receipts and an optional emailed copy. Assignments (set work, hand in online, grade with feedback) and a past-questions library (PDF papers students can search and download) are in Pro; timed computer-based exams (question bank, random questions, several subjects in one exam with free movement between them, automatic marking, scores sent to the results) are in Pro too, all in the same Classroom Suite
  • Text-message (SMS) password reset for students, parents and staff; people choose Email or SMS on the reset screen

Pro functionality is not included in this WordPress.org build.

External services

This plugin uses Freemius, a licensing and software-update platform, to manage optional license activation for the Pro version and (only if you choose to opt in) anonymous usage analytics that help us improve the plugin.

No data is sent to Freemius automatically when the plugin is activated. On first activation you’re shown a one-time opt-in screen with two options — “Skip” or “Allow & Continue” — and nothing is transmitted to Freemius until you make that choice. If you click “Skip”, no usage data is shared and the plugin works fully. If you click “Allow & Continue”, or if you later connect a license or account from the Account page, the following is sent: your site URL, WordPress and PHP version, this plugin’s version, and (for connecting an account) the name and email of the WordPress user connecting it. No student, teacher, parent, or school data stored by this plugin (results, attendance, admission numbers, PINs, etc.) is ever sent to Freemius or any other third party — all of that stays in your own WordPress database.

Pro version only, and only if you turn it on: SMS password/PIN reset. When an administrator selects Twilio or Africa’s Talking and enters their own account details, the plugin sends the recipient’s phone number and a short text containing a one-time code to that provider when someone asks for an SMS reset (and to the number you type when you press “Send test SMS”). Nothing is sent until you choose a provider and enable it, and no results or other school data is included.
Twilio: https://www.twilio.com — Terms: https://www.twilio.com/legal/tos — Privacy: https://www.twilio.com/legal/privacy
Africa’s Talking: https://africastalking.com — Terms: https://africastalking.com/terms — Privacy: https://africastalking.com/privacy

Pro version only, and only if you turn it on: online admission payments. When an administrator enables Stripe, PayPal or Paystack and a parent chooses to pay online, the plugin sends the fee amount, currency, the parent’s email address and the application reference to that provider, and the parent completes payment on the provider’s own page. The plugin later asks the provider whether the payment succeeded. Nothing is sent until you enable a provider and a parent starts a payment.
